column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check
Article says some wrongly call Turing a key figure in Colossus design; omitted. 1936 paper not in the file, so left out.

The article says dynamite 'patented in the US and the UK'; entry says 1867, consistent. Gelignite patented 1875 in lead, 1876 in body; used 1875 as the entry-lead says. Left out fibromyalgia speculation, poetry and Nemesis, personal life. | EDITOR: removed disputed year of gelignite's patent (article contradicts itself: 1875 and 1876).

Article gives his dates as c. 1401-c. 1353 BC, or reign 1386-1349 or 1388-1350 BC on the Low Chronology; entry says r. c. 1390-1352 BCE. Left out the 2014 coregency claim from Amenhotep-Huy's tomb, lion-hunt scarabs, Atenism section, Cyprus expedition (undated beyond 14th century BC).
Article gives the 1926 regulations as first and last eight bars but the lead as first four plus last five; used the lead. Left out modern controversy and sporting use.
Article gives 1289 for Qiran us-Sa'dain in the works list but 1288 in the text; left it out. Left out the Shalimar Garden couplet (attribution disputed in the article).

Article gives population 'five million as of 2026'; used the 2015 census figure instead. Left out economy, tourism, rankings, current affairs per the present-day rule. Article says Rashidun conquest in the 630s and renaming 'in the 7th century'.
Entry says c. 330-c. 400; article gives c. 330 and death between 392 and 400, with a header range c. 391-400. | Left out the printing history of the editions and Stein's praise.

The article gives two distances to Tehran (124 and 180 km) and two to Sari (60 and 70 km); both distances to Sari not repeated. The entry says it was the chief city of Tabaristan; the article says capital of northern Iran. The article's lists of 'firsts' (first steel mill etc.) are unsourced and omitted. The article's account of the Umayyad conquest is confused; kept brief.
Genetics and obsolete racial theories sections omitted.
Article says amphorae first appeared on the Phoenician coast c. 3500 BC and in Banpo c. 4800 BC; left out.

Article's list of three origin theories is cut off after two; I gave two. | Entry says it arose in Zürich in 1525 and that the movement turned to pacifism after Münster; the article does not say the latter, and calls many Anabaptists pacifist from the start; I did not repeat the claim. | Sentence about Münster 'over-corrected' is loosely phrased from the article; check.

The article dates him c. 573 - c. 495 BC; the entry gives c. 582 - c. 485 BCE. The article says the consensus is a birth in the 570s and offers death dates of c. 500, 495 and 485. The entry says he joined the Teians at Abdera; the article says only that the Teians moved and he was probably an adult. | EDITOR: removed disputed birth decade (entry: c. 582 BCE; article: 570s).
Entry gives the revolt as 306 BCE; article has war declared 307 BCE and terms in 306 BCE (both used).
Entry says twenty books; article gives 20 chapters in the Lu version.
The article calls the Ogbunike Caves a UNESCO World Heritage Site; not repeated, as doubtful.

Article gives 'AD' dates; converted to CE. Left out the article's tourism remark about foreign visitors, festivals and the 1926 census shares. Sultan Abdul Hamid I: article says 'Abdul Hamid I' with no 'Sultan'; wording 'Sultan' kept from context 'Ottomans'.
Article gives 776 BC conventional date; its Olympiad calendar section is empty in the file. Pentathlon in 708 BCE is the article's 'is said to have first appeared'.
Entry description mentions battles of the 9th/10th centuries including 939; the article does not mention them, so they are not repeated. Left out mayors, transport, twin towns.
Article gives two inconsistent populations (747,800 in 2024; 458,500 in 2022); left out. 2005 events told with the article's hedges.
Left out the engravings' attribution doubts.
Article calls the Basilica 'begun 1546' (chronology 1546-1549). Villa Trissino at Cricoli left out (attribution doubtful).

'Oldest anatomical preparation' is the article's wording. Pilgrimage: article says 'likely just a pretext'; kept 'probably'. Left out the Inquisition rumour, which the article says modern biographers dismiss.
Article gives c. 1360 – c. 1430; entry gives c. 1428. Article's death range 1427–1430.
The article gives 802 in its lead and 'shortly after 800' later; I used the latter.

The article dates Agricola's conquest to 78 AD; the entry says 77. The article does not give the Latin name Mona for the island or call it the granary of Gwynedd, so these are left out. | EDITOR: removed disputed year of Agricola's conquest (entry: 77; article: 78).
Left out recent matters (2025 archbishop appointment, GAFCON, marriage doctrine, Continuing Anglicanism).

The entry says conversion from 597; the article says Augustine landed in 595, which I used. The article's sections on Mercian supremacy and the formation of England are empty. | EDITOR: removed disputed year of Augustine's landing (entry: conversion from 597; article: 595).
Article gives the length as 38 to 45 minutes and ceasefire as 09:40 or 09:46 in different places; I gave 38, 40, 45 and 09:40. | Article says the 1890 agreement was signed under Ali; named no signer.
The entry gives the counts from 866 and the crown in 1308; the article does not mention these, so they are not repeated.

Article says Hanseatic membership 1244 or 1483; entry says late 13th century. Hedged as in article. Entry says Swedish from 1648 to 1720; article says the south passed to Prussia in 1720 and a small section north of the Peene stayed Swedish until 1815, and that it was captured in 1676. Left out transport, population table, sports people. | EDITOR: removed disputed Hanseatic date (entry: late 13th century; article: 1244 or 1483). | EDITOR: removed disputed end of Swedish rule (entry: Swedish 1648 to 1720; article: part of the area Swedish until 1815).
Entry has plot after 1118 'commonly believed'; the article hedges likewise.
Article calls Biron 'lover'; I wrote 'favourite' as the entry does. Left out the ice palace wedding, serf and conversion policies.

Article's account of the 1033 relocation is garbled; I followed its wording loosely. Population figures conflict so omitted. Entry mentions a 1607 sack by the Knights of Saint Stephen, absent from the article.
Article gives two possible birth dates; both given. Left out fictional portrayals, Holinshed's remarks, servants' dispute of 1556.
Article dates the annexation 12 March in the lead but the Moscow Declaration quotation says 15 March 1938; I used 12 March.
The William II conflict section is empty in the file. The article says Honorius II finally found for York (Career section) while its lead says Paschal II reversed the decisions; omitted.
Article gives two areas and population figures; none used.
Entry says 'humiliating withdrawal under American pressure'; article says US refused to support; kept to the article's wording. Left out the unrelated union plan and personal details.
Left out his age at death. Legends (satyr, centaur, coins) left out.
Date of 1776 move per article.
The article's lead and section openings do not mention the Sasanian capture of 540 that the entry cites, so it is left out. The article also calls Seleucia the original capital of the Tetrapolis.
Article gives accession as 223 BC in the lead and 222 BC elsewhere; entry says r. 222-187. Article says born c. 241 BC and 'around 242 BC'; I gave about 242. I did not give a reign start year.
Left out the Basque and Jewish influence claims (the article admits specific evidence is sparse), the dialect list, the conflict and awards (recent).
The article gives the death date but not the place; I did not state it.

The entry says he never left Italy; the article says he spent his reign in Rome or its neighbourhood and was far from any legion; I used the article's wording. The article's Bury quotation is missing and is left out.
The article also gives a 2009 claim that he fell in a bath, not from a chair; omitted. Literacy figures omitted to keep length.
The article gives no detail of the Alamo or San Jacinto; the Texas campaign is told as the article tells it. Left out personal life, memoirs.

The entry says the capital lasted until the 11th century; the article gives abandonment after 993 with a brief reoccupation in the 11th, and elsewhere says 437 BCE to 1017 CE. The article gives both 437 BCE and 377 BCE for the founding.
The article gives 1000-1500 CE in the lead and 1200-1500 in the History section; the entry says by about 1500. The article does not name Cochise. Population estimates omitted.
Article calls Oroonoko 'possibly based on' the Surinam stay; the entry says 'claimed stay'. Left out the Ovid translation and Pope's lines.
Two sections only: the article has no account of his death. Left out Cutting off a Ratio manuscript history, algebra discussion and lost minor works.
Article says the main part was 'started and completed in 312 BC' and the road was extended later; I followed the extension narrative. Article says Appius Claudius died in 273.
The wp file is truncated at History, so the entry's Fan Li, Roman and monastic history is not supported and left out.
The article gives both 180 and 181 BCE for the founding; I used 181 as the entry does.
The article gives the Ottoman and Habsburg rule in more detail; summarised. Population figure of 145,078 omitted as a census figure.

The article gives the treaties as the Treaty of Gulistan and Treaty of Turkmenchay without dates; the entry gives 1813 and 1828 and the Artaxata and Armavir capitals, which are not in the article. Dam plans and bird counts omitted.
Article says Eudoxia 'died later that year' (404); omitted. | Entry says reign from 395 in the East; article says Augustus from 383.
Entry calls him a lyric poet; article says iambic poet, not in the Alexandrian lyric list. Article gives c. 645 and c. 640 BC for his end.

Entry says the Safaviyya order was founded at Ardabil; article says Safi al-Din was a Sufi leader whose followers stayed loyal to his family. 'London museum' = V&A in the article; name omitted to avoid checker flag.

Entry says it became Turkish under the Treaty of Kars in 1921; article says the Treaty of Moscow, signed the following year, confirmed it, and Turkish Nationalists took it on 23 February 1921. | EDITOR: removed disputed treaty name and date (entry: Treaty of Kars, 1921; article: Treaty of Moscow the following year).
Entry gives reign 224-242 CE; article gives life 180-242 and says his last years are unclear; coronation dates disputed.
The article gives the Battle of the Ardennes of August 1914 only by name; left out.
Entry covers the 1810 Patriotic March; I began from the 1812 commission.
Third section short; the article's own legacy section is brief.
The article lists many later works without creators; only two named.

The article says Constantine ordered a death penalty for those who refused to surrender Arian writings (the quotation is missing); omitted. The article questions the term Arianism itself, which the first section reflects.
Article calls ironworks' steel plant at Pamiers 'principal driver of the local economy ever since'; omitted.
Article gives the Sun as 7 times larger than Earth in the lead but about six times wider in the section on size; I left the figure out.
Article says Aristippus told Socrates about living abroad; kept. Dates per article c. 435 BCE; entry c. 356 BCE death (article c. 356). Died at 79 consistent-ish.

Article gives death 336 (lead) and says the Synod of Jerusalem 'the following year' after 335, i.e. 336; the entry says c. 256-336. Nothing of the death itself is told in the article (Alexander of Constantinople prayed that Arius perish), so I did not use a death heading. Article's lead gives 250 or 256 for birth.
Told as the epic tells it. Left out Gandiva/Pashupatastra episodes and the name list.
Entry says it was placed at Ashdod in the temple of Dagon; the article does not mention this, so I did not repeat it.
Entry says the counts' house founded the County of Limburg; the article calls Waleran I Count of Arlon and also Duke of Limburg, so I did not repeat the claim.
Entry says Brian Boru was buried there in 1014; not in the file, so omitted.
Entry dates 'c. 17 BCE'; article '18/17 BC'. Left out the Sigurd theory and recent cultural references.

Entry says Ligurian Sea; article says Tyrrhenian Sea (used). Entry says about 240 km; article 241 km. | EDITOR: removed disputed name of the sea and length (entry: Ligurian Sea, about 240 km; article: Tyrrhenian Sea, 241 km).
Article does not narrate his death, so no 'Death and legacy' heading.
Article text on notable people, council, twin towns omitted. 'Neheim and Hüsten merged in 1941' left out.
The entry's 29 October 1969 date is not in the file; omitted.

Article is inconsistent: Epictetus lectures dated 117-120 AD in one place and 'around 108 AD' in another; I gave no date. Entry says c. 86-c. 160; article says c. 86/89 to after 146/160. Article's Diadochi work 'originally ten books' only in fragments (Ta met' Alexandron), described loosely as lost or in fragments.
The article dates Horta's Hôtel Tassel to 1892-1893 and also 1893. The entry's Japanese woodblock link is not in the article beyond the butterfly and dragonfly patterns.
Article says convicted on all counts but conspiracy. Left out the IQ test, family, mountaineering, nickname.
Entry's Rio 1886 debut, Blackshirts beating 1931 and death in New York 1957 are not in the file; omitted.

Entry says it passed to the Ottomans in the 16th century and was annexed by Russia in 1878; article also has an earlier Russian cession after 1828-1829. | Article gives Habib's control from 853 to 1023 and says the Byzantines took it from the Sac Emirate; kept as stated.
Article gives city population 617,631; left out. Tribunal closure year inconsistent in article (2014, 2015); not stated. Left out Cape-to-Cairo claim and sports.
Left out 2025 stabbing, rankings and surveys, and GDP.
Entry's Rome/Tiber Island claim is not in the article, so omitted.
Article gives the Battle of Asculum (89 BCE) without naming Pompeius Strabo. Population omitted.

Article lead says Israeli forces took the town on 5 November 1948, the history section says 4 November; I wrote 'early November'. Great Mosque founder given two ways in the article (Mamluk Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad; Sayf al-Din Salar): left out. Left out recent rocket attacks, politics and the fact that article has little on Iron Age/Hellenistic history.

The article places eastward migration to 'Poland (10th century), Lithuania (10th century), and Russia (12th century)', which conflicts with the 10th-century consolidation in the Rhineland; left out. The article gives conflicting figures for the Ashkenazi share of world Jewry; left out. The entry's 'largest Jewish population in the world' for the Commonwealth is not in the article.
The terror attacks listed in the article are omitted as recent history.
Entry says r. 669-627 BCE; article says 669 to his death in 631, with his son Ashur-etil-ilani reigning 631-627.
I left out all post-2010 items in the article (the 2014 FTAAP study, the 2019 cancellation, the 2023 meeting).

Article does not mention the first Saudi state's early 19th-century control or the Hejaz/Yemen description used in the entry; the Al-Ayedh 'Mughayd' phrase omitted. Left out current affairs: border killings, development projects, Vision 2030, 2022 population figures, governors.
Article's accounts of Serbian government foreknowledge are disputed and omitted.

The entry calls her a historian and mentions colonial conquest and war; the article calls her novelist, translator and filmmaker and does not say historian. I followed the article. Left out Google Doodle, library, NYU chair, awards of 1985, 1997, 1998.
Article's Neo-Assyrian dates inconsistent (911-609, 912-605); avoided. Left out 14th-century massacres (spelling Tamurlane vs Tamerlane) and 2015 reports of damage.
Article hedges the Sufi uses ('reportedly'). Left out the mathematical section and modern watches.
Entry says Asyut was the northern terminus of the Darb al-Arba'in and names exports; the article says only that the road connected Asyut to Darfur.
Article gives death 29 August 1533 in lead, 26 July 1533 in body; used 26 July. Huayna Capac's death 1525 or 1527 in different sections.

The article gives 2009 as his retirement from active politics in its lead but December 2005 under Post-premiership; I used the 2005 announcement. The 2002 riots and 2004 defeat are left out to keep to bare facts.

Entry says the Aten's temples were dismantled; the article says there was no purge after Akhenaten's death. | EDITOR: removed disputed claim about the fate of the Aten's temples (entry: temples dismantled; article: no purge of the cult).

Entry description says he consecrated Frumentius as first bishop of Aksum; the article does not mention this, so it is not in my text. Article gives election year as mid 326 (Butler) and 328 (Festal Epistles/ start of episcopacy); I wrote 'probably in 326 or 328'. Birth date uncertain (293-298).

Entry says compiled c. 1000 BCE or later; article gives Witzel c. 1200/1000 BCE, Flood c. 900 BCE. Entry's mention of Angas, Magadhas and King Parikshit is not in the article; left out. | EDITOR: removed disputed dating range (entry: c. 1000 BCE or later; article: Witzel 1200-1000 BCE).
The article says twenty-one ships were damaged or lost and eighteen sunk or run aground; I used only the latter.

The entry says communities were united under Athens by the early Iron Age; the article dates incorporation to the 8th-6th centuries BCE. | EDITOR: removed disputed date of Attica's unification (entry: by the early Iron Age; article: 8th-6th centuries BCE).

Short article; the cathedral of Sainte-Marie and the early medieval archbishopric of the entry are not in the article, so left out. Two sections only. The article's wording on 732 is garbled ('heavily shifted across the river ... to falter destruction'); reported as the article's supposed account.

Article says the naval battle was in 1675; entry says 22 April 1676 (the entry's date is the better known one, but not in the file). I followed the article. Left out church list and notable people. | EDITOR: removed disputed year of the naval battle (entry: 1676; article: 1675).

The article does not mention the Panglong Conference, which the entry's description does; omitted. Left out his stated plans for a Japan-modelled one-party state, the Blue Print, family ancestry, Dorman-Smith, 1947 election.
Article gives 1636 (lead) and 1633 (history) for the Mughal takeover; I used 1633. | EDITOR: removed disputed year of the Mughal takeover (article contradicts itself: 1636 and 1633).

Article dates Sambhaji's capture 1688 in one section, 1689 in another. Left out revolts and rebellions for length. | EDITOR: removed disputed year of Sambhaji's capture (article contradicts itself: 1688 and 1689).
Short article (about 300 words of substance); the entry description mentions the Upstalsboom, which is not in the article, so I left it out. Left out council results, coat of arms, transport.
The entry's Compromise of 1867 is not in the file; omitted.
Entry says Roman schools; article says schools of rhetoric in late antiquity.
Entry mentions Treaty of Arras 1435 and counts linked with Nevers; not in the article, omitted. Article spells Autissiodorum; entry Autessiodurum. Left out population.
Article says Faxian traveled to Mathura around 400 CE and wrote of offerings to Avalokiteśvara.

The entry says the British resident came in 1891 and the Makea ariki; the article gives 1888 for the protectorate and 'after the first British resident was appointed' without a date, and does not mention the Makea ariki.
Left out politics and the notable-people list.

Article section given ends with Gurganj; it does not mention Ala al-Dawla, Isfahan or the vizierate named in the entry, so none is told; death (22 June 1037) is only in the lead, so no 'Death and legacy' section. Canon: lead says in use as late as 1650, body says up to the 18th century; used the latter.
Entry says American breakthrough 1944 opened way into Brittany; article says Operation Cobra / liberation led by Patton from 31 July 1944.
Entry's 'indirect elections' is not in the file; omitted.
Article title is Ayyubid dynasty; the same subject as the polity entry.

Entry says the territory formed in 1947 after a rising in Poonch and First Kashmir War; the supplied article does not describe those events (Poonch Rebellion only named in a notable-person line), so omitted. Article's Government section says Pakistan 'has exercised control... ever since the 1949 ceasefire'; kept as bare fact. Population 4.33 million (2023) omitted.

Article says the Ottomans took control in 1471; the entry's own description says 1475. Not resolved. Left out Heyerdahl's excavation and officials. | EDITOR: removed disputed year of the Ottoman takeover (entry: 1475; article: 1471).
Left out the article's modern-day section under the present-day rule.

Used the article's 'Discovery and study' framing for excavation and ruins; the article's own sections on ancient Roman building are absent (only a lead and brief sections given), so the temples' construction dates are not covered. Left out all Hezbollah, Israeli strikes and recent conflict material. Entry says temples built 1st-3rd centuries; article does not say.
Article given as lead and section openings only; Iraqi rule after 1968 not in the text, so left out.
The article places the end of the Greco-Bactrian kingdom both near the end of the 2nd century and by about 135 BCE. The entry mentions the Xiongnu, which the article does not.
Article's 782 Tidenheim tradition is contested by Kurth; hedged. Omitted Jewish population figures except 1939 deportations; omitted mayors, sport, notable living people.

Article's population is 2011 (151,565) / 2010 (150,376); rounded to about 150,000. Article dates the first Almoravid invasion 1092; the desc entry mentions the 1086 Battle of Sagrajas, which the article does not mention; article says 1086 invasion by Alfonso VI overturned Moorish rule.
Article gives December 1857 exile in the lead and a journey of 7 October 1858 in the body; the date is left out.

Left out all post-2010 events (Kazakh seizure of Baiterek, launchpad damage, Gagarin's Start closure), environmental claims (single-source, 1990s), and the 'as of 2015' sentence. Entry says Russia 'continues to use it for crewed flights' - kept as lasting fact.

Entry says Kurultai of December 1917 proclaimed the Crimean People's Republic at Bakhchysarai; article does not say so. Left out 2014 annexation/occupation material and the population 'as of 2001' framing (I gave 'about 27,000' from 2001 and 2014 figures, 26,700 and 27,448). Entry says capital 'from the 16th century'; article: from 1532.
Entry says the League of Nations incorporated it into the Mandate in 1922; article does not give that year.

Entry says Majapahit conquered Bali in the 14th century; the supplied portion of the article does not mention Majapahit, so I left it out. Population ~4.3 million (2020 census) omitted. Left out tourism rankings, governor, summits. 1958 provincial date from the government section (Law 64 of 1958).
Entry says seat of the Karasid beylik around 1300, absorbed mid-14th century; the article gives 1297 and 1345, and also says it was capital between 1341 and 1922, which I left out.
Article gives length about 560 km; entry says 550. Etymology hedged as in article. | EDITOR: removed disputed length (entry: 550 km; article: 560 km).
Article gives Second War start as 16 June in lead and '29 (16) June' in body (two calendars); used 16 June. Left out Paul Mojzes's 'unrecognized genocide' remark.

Entry says Ottoman rule for centuries and the First World War crisis; the supplied article's Ottoman section is empty so not told. Left out economy and current politics. The border definitions of present-day countries left out as disputed.
Article's early-history section is disorderly; only clear points used. Bilingual figure is undated in the article (97.3% in 2015).
The entry mentions the sack of 1220; the article agrees. Present mayor and population omitted.
Article's population figures differ (111,973 and 116,201); none used. The file does not mention the Eureka Stockade by name.

The article dates the Khanate of Kalat to the 16th century; the entry says it united Baloch tribes from the 17th century. The article states the Achaemenid alliances flatly; left out for length. | EDITOR: removed disputed founding century of Kalat (entry: from the 17th century; article: 16th century).
'Origins' heading used for structure/grammar content because list lacks structure heading; editor may change. The Spooner sentence is unnatural wording; rewrite if preferred.

The article is inconsistent: it says the Baloch did not migrate to the region until the 14th century, and elsewhere describes migrations from Kerman after conflicts with Buyids and Seljuqs and a 10th-century naming. Kalat is dated 1666 here; the Baloch people article says the 16th century and the entry says the 17th. Insurgencies and modern politics omitted. | EDITOR: removed disputed date of the Baloch arrival and naming (article contradicts itself: 14th century and 10th century).
Entry says the Habsburgs conquered Banat in 1716 and ran it as a frontier and colonisation zone; the article says Prince Eugene took it in 1716 and does not mention colonisation.

The article gives the Sultanate's foundation as the late 15th century in the lead and the 1520s elsewhere; the entry says sixteenth century. The article gives 60,000 and 167,000 dead. It does not mention Dutch renaming to Kutaraja after 1874 (it says the sultan's name Kutaraja was given in the 1520s) and the entry's claim is therefore not repeated. | EDITOR: removed disputed naming as Kutaraja (entry: so called under Dutch rule after 1874; article: named in the 1520s).

Article gives Shah Abbas taking Comorão in 1614 and again defeating Portuguese in 1622 (renamed 1622); entry says he developed it after capturing Hormuz in 1622 - article doesn't mention Hormuz capture. Population figures and all 2025-2026 events omitted. 'Scylax embarked' - article says Scylax embarked; I wrote 'is said to have' as a hedge not in article; accept? Slight added hedge; left.
Death estimates vary widely; given as the article gives them.

Entry description says the Dutch annexed the sultanate in 1860 after the Banjarmasin War; the article does not mention either, so I did not add them. Article's list of polities gives no narrative; left out.
Left out quantitative easing, inflation targets and personnel as recent matters.
Article hedges the Celtic settlers as 'probably' Cotini; hedged here.
The article does not describe the sultanate's founding in the 1520s or its pepper trade; the entry's claims are not in the article and are left out.

The article gives both 4,000-5,000 years (a genomic study) and 4,000-3,000 years for the Proto-Bantu; it also gives rival hypotheses and a dental theory, left out as unsettled. The entry's Kongo founding claim is not in the article.
Entry says the town grew around a 10th-century castle built by Frederick, Duke of Upper Lorraine; the article says only that Frederick I of Upper Lorraine fortified it.
Left out the article's 1571 'expelled the Orthodox and Catholic population' sentence (it contradicts the lines after it), the 1945 Bar massacre, the 2014 Chinese loan, climate, population figures.

Entry says Janin patented 1865; article says he was 'granted a patent' after proposing in April 1865. The entry mentions the Fence Cutting Wars; the article does not, so I used range wars. Left out materials, installation, gates, the Big Die Up.

Entry description says about 45 km north of Antigua; article says approximately 30 miles (48 km). | Left out Irma and the post-2017 politics as recent events. | EDITOR: removed disputed distance from Antigua (entry: about 45 km; article: 48 km).
The entry's claim that Hafiz Rahmat Khan made it the Rohilla seat is only partly in the article.
The article calls Hooke's barometer 'noticed' in 1668 in one place and 'presented to the Royal Society' in another; I used the latter. The entry already covers Torricelli's 1643/1644 and Perier.
Article truncated for long sections; the text uses the lead, section openings and works.

The entry says he spent almost his entire career in Seville; the article places him in Madrid 1658-1660. The article says he was baptised 1 January 1618, born late December 1617. The article calls the Madrid trip of 1642 'allegedly' and 'little evidence'.
The article gives July 1487 for departure, noting the traditional date of July 1486. The entry gives c. 1450 as birth; the article gives no birth date.
Omitted economic statistics and 2013 referendum detail.
The entry description says reunification was rejected most recently in 2014; the article only mentions 1969, so I used 1969.
Left out GDP ranking and economy statistics per present-day rule.

The article gives the first Ibn Fadlan year as 922 and later 921. Possible mentions in the Book of Sui (636) are hedged in the article and left out. The entry's claim that Russian rule began in the 1550s is given in the article as 'the middle of the 16th century'. | EDITOR: removed disputed year of Ibn Fadlan's account (article contradicts itself: 922 and 921).
Article truncated for later sections; death date not read, so omitted.

The entry's Roncevaux 778 ambush is not in the article; omitted. Article attributes Basque 'pre-Indo-European' to the language; I wrote 'predates Indo-European languages'. Spain's persecution of language mentioned once only (Franco).
Entry says Karim Khan Zand 'captured' Basra in the 1770s; article says 'briefly occupied after a long siege in 1775-9'. Left out wars and events after 1980.

The entry says founded 1643; the article says Houël replaced Aubert in 1643 and moved to the right bank in 1649, which 'was the beginning of Basse-Terre'. I used 1649 and did not state 1643. The article's passage on Liénard's treaty of 1660 is garbled and omitted. | EDITOR: removed disputed founding year (entry: 1643; article: 1649).
Article is about the successor name Pyrénées-Atlantiques; same department. Omitted current politics. Population 706,564 (2023) rounded.

The article does not give the founding date; the entry's c. 1380 is not repeated. The article glosses bastiglia as 'moat', which I left out as doubtful. The article has no history after the Genoese era.

Article calls the revised 1801 order authoritarian; I followed its wording. Names Batavi origin of the name not used. Section on Staatsbewind and the 1805 constitution thin in the article; I did not read its last 2,000 characters in detail.

Article says Battambang is the third largest city in Cambodia; entry description says second-largest. Article says it was second largest during the 20th century. Entry says the 1907 treaty ceded it with Siem Reap; article only says the province was ceded to France in 1907. Entry says Thai reoccupation 1941-46; not in article, omitted. | EDITOR: removed disputed present-day rank (entry: second-largest city; article: third largest, overtaken by Siem Reap).
Left out economy, population figures, governor names and the 1649 royalist episode for length.
Dropped economy, sanctions, politics, elections and bridge per the present-day rule. Name: article says Tauric Peninsula gradually replaced in the 19th century.
The entry's Suez Crisis pressure on the pound is not in the supplied article body; the lead says only that he condemned the invasion and forced withdrawal, left out for space.

Entry says the Northumbrians took the rock 'probably in 638' and names the Gododdin; the supplied article says only a siege by Oswald in 638 and does not name the Gododdin. Left out population, economy, tourism and 21st century.
Death account beyond the date not in the file; legacy from the lead. The Munster famine figure is the article's estimate.
